```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness-to-pay is better evidenced in A. Several sourced competitor price points ($119-$199 Expatfile, $175 MyExpatTaxes, $169+$49 H&R Block, $199-$799+ Atamatax) and a sourced Reddit quote of $800-$2,500 accountant fees point to a market paying hundreds of dollars a year. B's price ceiling is $1-4/month.",
    "A's demand quotes come from the target segment itself (r/USExpatTaxes, r/ExpatFIRE, r/AmericanExpatsUK). B's demand quotes come from general mail-client support forums (Zoho, Apple, Microsoft), not from the privacy-conscious alias users it names as payers.",
    "B's own brief says the exact feature is already shipped by five competitors. Three of them include it free or cheap, and a free open-source Thunderbird extension covers the client-side case. That leaves no sourced reason a user would pay for a standalone tool.",
    "A has a narrower fallback that can plausibly win a first customer in 90 days: a US-side, PFIC/FBAR-aware product for a single country pairing. The Atamatax example shows a one-person build can occupy this kind of niche. B has no comparable whitespace identified.",
    "A's risks (EFIN authorization, liability, the multi-country local-filing scope) are serious, but they are scope and execution risks. B's core risk is near-absent willingness to pay, which is harder to overcome within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence does not match its payer. The three forum quotes come from users of Zoho, Apple Mail, and Outlook, and two of them describe business or admin aliases (main/info addresses). None shows a privacy-conscious prosumer with many aliases wanting this as a separate paid product. The brief itself leaves the size of the 10+ alias segment and its willingness to pay as open questions.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's case has its own gaps. The claim that Atamatax 'attracts customers' is not backed by any customer or revenue evidence. The EFIN approval timeline is unknown and could block e-filing within 90 days. The idea's stated differentiator, local-country filing, is likely infeasible in scope. A wins mainly because B's evidence argues against a paid standalone product, not because A's path to a paying customer is proven."
}
```
